validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real and correctly classified. The cited Arabic source (Almasry Alyoum, 29-12-2010, 'مبارك يفتتح خط غاز الصعيد في أسوان الخميس') gives the full South Valley Gas Pipeline's 6-phase build-out (Dahshur->Aswan, 930km total, ~LE5.7bn), and explicitly names phase 4 as 'أبو قرقاص' (Abu Qurqas) to 'أسيوط' (Asyut governorate), 147km, 32-inch diameter -- an exact, segment-specific match to GEM's values for P6700, not a generic blanket citation. This same source's phase breakdown maps 1:1 onto all six GEM 'South Valley Gas Pipeline' rows (P6697 Dahshour-Giza 90km/36in = phase1 Dahshur-El Korimat; P6698 Al Kurimat-Beni Suef 30km/32in = phase2; P6699 Beni Suef-Minya 150km/32in = phase3 Beni Suef-Abu Qurqas; P6700 Abu Qurqas-Asyut 147km/32in = phase4 [this row]; P6701 Asyut-Sohag 121km/32in = phase5 Asyut-Girga; P6702 Girga-Aswan 390km/30in = phase6), confirming the 6-way segmentation is a faithful, non-duplicative rendering of the source's own staging -- no duplicate/double-count concern. Note the automated ref-check flagged 'operating' not found in the source text -- false negative: the article is Arabic and never uses the English word; substantively it describes the Dec-2010 presidential inauguration of the completed line, which supports operating status. Cross-checked against the GulfPub PE World Map 'South Valley Gas Pipeline' Abu Qurqus->Asyut candidate match (green 0.9385): GulfPub lists dia=32in (matches) but len_km=91, flagged as a 38% delta. Traced this: EVERY one of GulfPub's six South Valley segments is ~1.61x shorter than the matching GEM segment (Dahshur-ElKoraimet 56 vs GEM 90; ElKoraimet-BeniSuef 19 vs 30; BeniSuef-AbuQurqus 93 vs 150; AbuQurqus-Asyut 91 vs 147 [this row]; Asyut-Gerga 75 vs 121; Gerga-Aswan 242 vs 390) -- a strikingly consistent ratio of 1.607-1.616, i.e. essentially the mile-to-km conversion factor (1.60934). This is almost certainly a GulfPub unit-mislabeling bug (their 'len_km' column for this pipeline family is actually miles): 91mi x 1.60934 = 146.4km, which matches GEM's 147km almost exactly. So the apparent 38% spec conflict is not a real disagreement -- once corrected, GulfPub independently corroborates GEM's 147km. SPEC caveat (not material): two English trade-press pieces -- The Australian Pipeliner (23-Sep-2009, 'Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline reaches Sohag') and Petroleum Africa (3-Jan-2011, 'Mubarak Inaugurates Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline') -- both describe this same segment as 'stage three...136 km...32 inch...from the governorate of Minya to Assiut', i.e. 136km vs GEM's 147km (~7.5% lower). These two English pieces are NOT independent of each other (identical stage figures and quotes strongly suggest a shared wire/press-release lineage), so together they count as roughly one lineage, versus the specific, ministry-linked Arabic source (147km) that names this exact segment and is corroborated by the unit-corrected GulfPub figure. Net: 2 independent lineages support 147km/32in; 1 (non-independent-internally) lineage gives 136km. Under the 10% materiality bar this is not flagged as a hard spec conflict, but noting it for the record. ATTRIBUTION: GEM's Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100%, sourced to the same Almasry Alyoum article, which does list EGAS among the entities that participated in construction/execution of the trunk (alongside South Valley holding co, GASCO, Petrojet, Enppi) -- Owner is reasonably defensible as the ultimate state holding company. However, the Operator field on the operators/owners tab (oo_sheet_row 5356) is currently BLANK. Pipeliner (2009) states the 930km pipeline was built 'for the Nile Valley Gas Company' (NVGC), and Petroleum Africa (2011) attributes the same project to NVGC's implementation; GulfPub's independent 2025 scrape lists operator='Nile Valley Gas Company' for this exact Abu Qurqus->Asyut segment. Two independent lineages (2009/2011 English trade coverage + 2025 GulfPub compilation) agree NVGC is the operating entity for this Upper Egypt trunk, distinct from EGAS as parent/holding owner -- see fills for a proposed Operator fill.

routes.corridor_desc: This is phase 4 of the six-phase South Valley Gas Pipeline (Dahshur->Aswan trunk, 930km total per the Dec-2010 inauguration source), running south along the Nile Valley from Abu Qurqas (a town in Minya Governorate, roughly midway between Minya city and the Minya/Asyut governorate boundary) to Asyut city, continuing the corridor established by the preceding segment P6699 (Beni Suef->Abu Qurqas) and feeding into the following segment P6701 (Asyut->Sohag). No independent source gives an exact right-of-way (river-east-bank vs west-bank, or specific km-post waypoints) beyond the two named endpoint towns and the general phase sequence, so only a loose corridor bound (the Nile Valley strip between the two named towns, length ~147km per source) can be defended -- NOT a surveyed route. The sheet's existing RouteNotes ('Nagwa: this is the full route of the pipeline which includes six segments') suggests any prior geometry attempt for this PID may have represented the FULL 930km trunk rather than just this 147km segment -- worth a human check in the routes repo before any route work, since RouteAccuracy is already 'no route' here.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoint town/city identities (Abu Qurqas, Minya Governorate -> Asyut, Asyut Governorate) are confirmed by the same segment-specific Almasry Alyoum passage used for Length/Location. Start/end coordinates given are standard, well-documented town/city-center coordinates (public geographic reference, e.g. consistent with GeoNames/Wikipedia locations for these two well-known Egyptian towns) -- NOT derived from any pipeline-specific survey or route source, so treat only as anchor points for a human corridor sketch, not as verified route geometry. No waypoints are sourced; none fabricated. Given only two named endpoints with no route-specific corroboration, 'low' is the ceiling this evidence supports.

summary: P6700 (South Valley Gas Pipeline, Abu Qurqas-Asyut) confirmed real, correctly classified as gas transmission, and not a duplicate -- its length/diameter (147km/32in) are exactly named in the cited ministry-linked Arabic source and independently corroborated by GulfPub once a consistent ~1.61x mile/km mislabeling across GulfPub's whole South Valley family is corrected; a minor (non-independent) English trade-press pair gives 136km instead, noted but not material. Attribution caveat: Operator field is blank and should be filled with Nile Valley Gas Company (2 independent lineages); Owner=EGAS remains supportable. Length and Location refs (previously blank) filled with the existing, segment-specific citation.
